overview: This is the yearly bill that sets spending limits and rules for U.S. intelligence agencies, such as the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), for the 2026 budget year; most dollar amounts are in a classified attachment. It turns the existing counterintelligence office (the unit that guards against foreign spying) into a National Counterintelligence Center with a Senate-confirmed director who would be the President's top adviser on counterintelligence. It bans the Chinese AI app DeepSeek from intelligence computer systems, adds rules on artificial intelligence security and on buying data from commercial sellers, and requires agencies to delete public or purchased information about Americans that they collect by accident. It also bars agencies from requiring political or ideological activism for hiring or promotion, and directs intelligence agencies to support Ukraine's efforts to defend and retake its territory from Russia unless the intelligence director finds a compelling reason not to. On November 28, 2025, the House Intelligence Committee reported it and it was placed on the House calendar for a floor vote.
for: Supporters say the bill gives intelligence agencies the funding and direction they need, strengthens defenses against foreign spying, and adds privacy safeguards by requiring agencies to purge information about Americans they collect by accident.
against: Critics say the bill's real spending levels stay classified and out of public view, and that its privacy limits on buying commercial data about Americans do not go far enough.
